subject: Post-call: Data retention options and PII scope (FinGuard)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@finguard.ai>, Marta López <marta.lopez@finguard.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Data retention options and PII scope (FinGuard)

Evan / Marta — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Call recap (short):
- Primary goal: ingest user banking chat transcripts to power personalization and anomaly detection features.
- Key concerns: PII minimization, data residency (EU subset), and limiting long-term storage of conversational KV/cache and request logs.
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, audit logs for access, and the ability to redact/suppress fields at ingestion.

Options we discussed (summary):
1) 0-retention (ephemeral): session-only inference with no persistent KV or request logs retained beyond real-time. Requires Private deployment or Dedicated instance with additional contract and engineering controls.
2) Short-window logs: configurable per-tenant retention (7 / 30 / custom days) for request metadata & logs; full conversation transcript can be masked or redacted on ingest.
3) Hybrid: store only non-PII embeddings and aggregated metrics; retain raw transcripts only for a narrow debugging window behind access controls.

Questions I promised to follow up on:
- Can Redwood guarantee that KV cache is never written to durable storage? (short answer below)
- What artifacts we can share to satisfy procurement / security?
- Estimated engineering timeline and cost delta for 0-retention pilot.

Short answers (high level):
- KV cache persistence: by default our hosted runtime keeps KV in memory, but we replicate/transmit caches for autoscaling and failover in the Hosted plan. For true 0-retention we offer a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated provisioning with a configuration to avoid writing caches to durable volumes and to disable cross-region replication. We will need a short engineering change to harden the path and provide an attestation for the customer.
- Artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report, data flow diagram (attached), sample KMS integration notes, and an access-log sample.
- Timeline / cost: a scoped 0-retention pilot (Dedicated with config changes + short security attestation) is typically 6–8 weeks and has incremental provisioning and engineering fees.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share a concise one-page summary of retention options and a dataflow diagram (attached).
2) Evan / Marta: confirm whether the EU residency requirement applies to all PII or to a subset of customer segments.
3) If you want to pursue 0-retention pilot, let me know and I’ll introduce you to our Private/Dedicated onboarding lead to scope costs and timeline.

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf, retention-options-summary.xlsx

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data retention options and PII scope (FinGuard)

Thanks Alex — clear recap, appreciated. Couple of clarifying points before we pull legal / security in: 

1) When you say KV cache can be "kept in memory" — can you confirm whether crash dumps or debug snapshots could ever contain unencrypted KV data? We need to ensure our legal team that nothing with direct PII can be recovered after a session.

2) Does the 6–8 week pilot timeline include time for our InfoSec to conduct an internal code review or is that separate? We will need the SOC 2 and any attestation to move to procurement.

3) On EU residency — yes, for now it applies to EU customers only (we have a sizeable EU merchant base). We'd prefer the data-in-region be enforced for PII-derived artifacts (embeddings and logs) but are open to storing non-PII metrics in US.

For procurement: procurement@finguard.ai — please hold until we confirm feasibility from InfoSec.

— Evan

Evan / Marta / team — following up with scoped answers and the artifacts Laura & Dev prepared. See attachments and notes below. Happy to jump on a short follow-up with InfoSec next week.

Summary answers (scoped):
- Crash dumps / debug snapshots: our runtime will not persist KV to disk in the Private deployment and we can disable non-essential crash dump collection for the dedicated tenant. For Hosted customers, we do capture minimal traces for debugging which are pseudonymized; by default those traces do not include raw KV contents. For your requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private to meet an explicit 0-retention contract.

- Attestation / artifacts attached: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), dataflow diagram (redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf), retention-options-summary.xlsx (includes pricing tiers and pilot estimate).

- EU residency: we can guarantee in-region storage for PII-derived artifacts (embeddings, logs) when you choose our EU Dedicated cluster or a Private VPC deployed in EU regions. Non-PII aggregated metrics may be stored in the US per your earlier comment.

- 0-retention pilot scoping:
  • Deployment: Dedicated EU cluster or Private VPC (customer choice)
  • Changes: disable durable KV persistence, disable cross-region replication, and apply automatic scrub/redact rules at ingress
  • Timeline: 6–8 weeks from SOW signature for dev/provisioning; pilot validation window 2 weeks.
  • Estimated incremental cost: one-time engineering integration + higher reserved capacity (detailed in attachment).

Suggested next steps:
1) Evan / Marta: please confirm whether you want Legal to see the attestation + pilot SOW (we can provide a redline-ready SOW).
2) If yes, we’ll schedule a 30–45 minute call with our Security lead (Laura) and Dev lead (Dev Patel) to walk through the attestation and the runtime configs.
3) Procurement: if you’re ready, we can share a draft SOW and pricing worksheet.

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf, retention-options-summary.xlsx

Thanks — Alex
